Auto
======

A collection of source code generators for [Java][java].

Auto‽
-----

[Java][java] is full of code that is mechanical, repetitive, typically untested and sometimes the source of subtle bugs. _Sounds like a job for robots!_

The Auto subprojects are a collection of code generators that automate those types of tasks. They create the code you would have written, but without the bugs.

Save time.  Save code.  Save sanity.

Subprojects
-----------

  * [AutoFactory](https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/factory) - JSR-330-compatible factories

    Latest version: `0.1-beta2`

  * [AutoService](https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/service) - Provider-configuration files for [`ServiceLoader`](http://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/ServiceLoader.html)

    Latest version: `1.0-rc2`

  * [AutoValue](https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/value) - Immutable [value-type](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Value_object) code generation for Java 1.6+.

    Latest version: `1.1`

  * [Common](https://github.com/google/auto/tree/master/common) - Helper utilities for writing annotation processors.

    Latest version: `0.4`

License
-------

    Copyright 2013 Google, Inc.

    Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    You may obtain a copy of the License at

       http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0

    WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
    See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
    limitations under the License.

[java]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_(programming_language)

# Maven Dependency Resolution

## Overview

### 1. Missing System Dependencies (tools.jar)
In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` was available in the JDK's `lib/` directory. However, in Java 9+, this was removed as the tools became part of the JDK modules.

**Problem**: Projects may reference `tools.jar` via system scope dependencies:
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

**Solution**: Remove or comment out the system-scoped tools.jar dependency when using Java 9+.

### 2. Profile-Based Dependencies
Maven profiles can conditionally include dependencies based on activation criteria like:
- OS detection
- JDK version
- File existence
- Environment variables

**Example**:
```xml
<profiles>
  <profile>
    <id>default-profile</id>
    <activation>
      <file>
        <exists>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</exists>
      </file>
    </activation>
    <dependencies>
      <!-- Dependencies activated when tools.jar exists -->
    </dependencies>
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

### 3. SNAPSHOT Dependencies
SNAPSHOT versions are development versions that can change. They require:
- Proper snapshot repository configuration
- Network access to snapshot repositories
- Or local installation via `mvn install`

## Maven Commands

### Build Commands
- `mvn clean` - Delete the target directory
- `mvn compile` - Compile source code
- `mvn test` - Run tests
- `mvn package` - Create JAR/WAR
- `mvn install` - Install to local repository (~/.m2/repository)
- `mvn clean install` - Full clean build and install

### Dependency Commands
- `mvn dependency:tree` - Show dependency tree
- `mvn dependency:resolve` - Resolve all dependencies
- `mvn dependency:analyze` - Analyze dependencies for issues

### Debugging
- `mvn -X` - Enable debug output
- `mvn -e` - Show full error stack traces

## Fixing Build Errors

### Step 1: Identify the Error
Look for error messages like:
- "Could not resolve dependencies"
- "Could not find artifact"
- "Failed to execute goal"

### Step 2: Check POM Files
Examine:
- Dependencies section
- Profiles section
- Properties section
- System-scoped dependencies

### Step 3: Apply Fixes
Common fixes:
1. Remove obsolete system dependencies
2. Update dependency versions
3. Build parent modules first (`mvn install` in parent)
4. Check repository accessibility

## Creating Diff Files

When fixing POM files, create standard diff format patches:

```diff
--- a/pom.xml
+++ b/pom.xml
@@ -10,7 +10,6 @@
   <dependencies>
-    <dependency>...</dependency>
   </dependencies>
```

Use unified diff format compatible with GNU diff and git.

# Java Version Compatibility

## Overview
Java has undergone significant changes between major versions, affecting how projects are built and what dependencies are available.

## Key Changes Between Java Versions

### Java 8 and Earlier
- JDK included `tools.jar` in `$JAVA_HOME/lib/`
- Contains compiler APIs and annotation processing tools
- Required for annotation processors
- Available as system-scoped dependency

### Java 9+ (Modular Java)
- Introduced Java Platform Module System (JPMS)
- `tools.jar` removed - functionality moved to modules
- Compiler API available via `javax.tools` module
- Annotation processing built into JDK

## Identifying Java Version

```bash
# Check Java version
java -version
javac -version

# Check JAVA_HOME
echo $JAVA_HOME

# List Java installations
ls /usr/lib/jvm/
```

## Common Version Compatibility Issues

### 1. tools.jar Dependencies
**Old Code (Java 8)**:
```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

**Fix for Java 9+**: Remove this dependency entirely. The compiler APIs are automatically available.

### 2. Source/Target Compatibility
Ensure Maven compiler plugin matches your Java version:

```xml
<properties>
  <maven.compiler.source>1.8</maven.compiler.source>
  <maven.compiler.target>1.8</maven.compiler.target>
</properties>
```

Or in compiler plugin:
```xml
<plugin>
  <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
  <configuration>
    <source>1.8</source>
    <target>1.8</target>
  </configuration>
</plugin>
```

### 3. Annotation Processing
For annotation processors in Java 9+, no special configuration needed. The `javax.annotation.processing.Processor` interface is available by default.

## Migration Strategies

### When Updating to Java 9+
1. Remove all `tools.jar` system dependencies
2. Update Maven compiler plugin to 3.8+
3. Review and update source/target versions
4. Test annotation processors work without tools.jar
5. Update profiles that check for tools.jar existence

## Version Detection in Maven

You can detect Java version in POMs:
```xml
<profile>
  <id>java9-plus</id>
  <activation>
    <jdk>[9,)</jdk>
  </activation>
  <!-- Configuration for Java 9+ -->
</profile>
```

## Best Practices

1. **Avoid system-scoped dependencies**: They're not portable
2. **Use properties for versions**: Centralize version management
3. **Test across Java versions**: Ensure compatibility
4. **Read migration guides**: Oracle provides detailed guides for each version

# Diff and Patch File Format

## Overview
Diff files (patches) describe changes between files. They're used for version control, code review, and applying fixes to codebases.

## Standard Unified Diff Format

The unified diff format is the most common and is used by Git and GNU diffutils.

### Basic Structure

```diff
--- a/path/to/original/file.ext
+++ b/path/to/modified/file.ext
@@ -start_line,num_lines +start_line,num_lines @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
 context line
```

### Header Lines
- `--- a/filename`: Original file (before changes)
- `+++ b/filename`: Modified file (after changes)

### Hunk Header
- `@@` markers delimit the hunk header
- `-start,count`: Line range in original file
- `+start,count`: Line range in modified file

### Content Lines
- ` ` (space): Context line (unchanged)
- `-`: Line removed from original
- `+`: Line added to modified
- `\`: No newline at end of file indicator

## Example: Removing Dependency from POM

```diff
--- a/factory/pom.xml
+++ b/factory/pom.xml
@@ -95,13 +95,6 @@
     </dependency>
-    <dependency>
-      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
-      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
-      <version>${java.version}</version>
-      <scope>system</scope>
-      <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
-    </dependency>
   </dependencies>
```

This shows:
- Modifying `factory/pom.xml`
- Starting at line 95 in original
- Removing 7 lines (the dependency block)
- Keeping context lines before and after

## Creating Diff Files

### Using diff command
```bash
diff -u original.txt modified.txt > changes.diff
```

### Using git
```bash
git diff > changes.diff
git diff --cached > staged-changes.diff
git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > last-commit.diff
```

### Manual Creation
1. Identify the file path (relative to repository root)
2. Write header with `---` and `+++`
3. Add hunk headers with line numbers
4. Show context (3 lines before/after is standard)
5. Mark removed lines with `-`
6. Mark added lines with `+`

## Applying Patches

### Using patch command
```bash
patch -p1 < changes.diff
# or
patch original.txt < changes.diff
```

### Using git
```bash
git apply changes.diff
git apply --check changes.diff  # dry run
```

### Flags
- `-p1`: Strip 1 directory level from paths (convert `a/file.txt` to `file.txt`)
- `-p0`: Keep full paths as-is
- `-R`: Reverse the patch
- `--dry-run`: Test without applying

## Best Practices

1. **Include context**: Shows where changes should be applied
2. **Use relative paths**: From repository root
3. **One logical change per file**: Or use multiple hunks
4. **Standard format**: Use unified diff (`-u` flag)
5. **Test patches**: Verify they apply cleanly
6. **Clear filenames**: Use descriptive patch names like `fix-maven-deps.diff`

## Multiple Files in One Patch

```diff
--- a/file1.txt
+++ b/file1.txt
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 line 1
-old line 2
+new line 2
 line 3
--- a/file2.txt
+++ b/file2.txt
@@ -1,2 +1,3 @@
 line 1
+new line 2
 line 3
```

## Common Issues

### Line Ending Differences
- Unix: LF (`\n`)
- Windows: CRLF (`\r\n`)
- Use `--ignore-whitespace` when applying patches

### Context Mismatch
- Patch fails if surrounding lines don't match
- Update context or use fuzzy matching (`-F` flag)

### Path Differences
- Adjust `-p` level to match directory structure
- Or edit patch file paths

## Verification

After creating a diff, verify it:
```bash
# Check the patch is valid
patch --dry-run -p1 < changes.diff

# Apply and test
patch -p1 < changes.diff
# Run builds/tests
# If needed: patch -R -p1 < changes.diff  # Revert
```

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.sonatype.oss</groupId>
    <artifactId>oss-parent</artifactId>
    <version>7</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
  <packaging>pom</packaging>
  <version>3</version>
  <name>Auto (Parent)</name>
  <description>A collection of code generators for Java.</description>
  <url>https://github.com/google/auto</url>

  <properties>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    <java.version>1.6</java.version>
  </properties>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <issueManagement>
    <system>GitHub Issues</system>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto/issues</url>
  </issueManagement>

  <licenses>
    <license>
      <name>Apache 2.0</name>
      <url>http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>
    </license>
  </licenses>

  <organization>
    <name>Google, Inc.</name>
    <url>http://www.google.com</url>
  </organization>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.1</version>
        <configuration>
          <source>${java.version}</source>
          <target>${java.version}</target>
          <compilerArgument>-Xlint:all</compilerArgument>
          <showWarnings>true</showWarnings>
          <showDeprecation>true</showDeprecation>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-checkstyle-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.11</version>
        <configuration>
          <consoleOutput>true</consoleOutput>
          <configLocation>checkstyle.xml</configLocation>
          <failOnViolation>false</failOnViolation>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
    <pluginManagement>
      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>1.8</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>
  </build>

  <profiles>
    <profile>
      <id>default-profile</id>
      <activation>
        <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>
        <file>
          <exists>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</exists>
        </file>
      </activation>
      <properties>
        <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>
      </properties>
    </profile>
    <profile>
      <id>mac-profile</id>
      <activation>
        <activeByDefault>false</activeByDefault>
        <file>
          <exists>${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar</exists>
        </file>
      </activation>
      <properties>
        <toolsjar>${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar</toolsjar>
      </properties>
    </profile>
  </profiles>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
	<modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

	<groupId>org.sonatype.oss</groupId>
	<artifactId>oss-parent</artifactId>
	<version>7</version>
	<packaging>pom</packaging>

	<name>Sonatype OSS Parent</name>
	<url>http://nexus.sonatype.org/oss-repository-hosting.html</url>
	<description>Sonatype helps open source projects to set up Maven repositories on https://oss.sonatype.org/ </description>

	<scm>
		<connection>scm:svn:http://svn.sonatype.org/spice/tags/oss-parent-7</connection>
		<developerConnection>scm:svn:https://svn.sonatype.org/spice/tags/oss-parent-7</developerConnection>
		<url>http://svn.sonatype.org/spice/tags/oss-parent-7</url>
	</scm>

	<repositories>
		<repository>
			<id>sonatype-nexus-snapshots</id>
			<name>Sonatype Nexus Snapshots</name>
			<url>https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots</url>
			<releases>
				<enabled>false</enabled>
			</releases>
			<snapshots>
				<enabled>true</enabled>
			</snapshots>
		</repository>
	</repositories>


	<distributionManagement>
		<snapshotRepository>
			<id>sonatype-nexus-snapshots</id>
			<name>Sonatype Nexus Snapshots</name>
			<url>${sonatypeOssDistMgmtSnapshotsUrl}</url>
		</snapshotRepository>
		<repository>
			<id>sonatype-nexus-staging</id>
			<name>Nexus Release Repository</name>
			<url>https://oss.sonatype.org/service/local/staging/deploy/maven2/</url>
		</repository>
	</distributionManagement>

	<build>
		<plugins>
			<plugin>
				<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
				<artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
				<version>1.0</version>
				<executions>
					<execution>
						<id>enforce-maven</id>
						<goals>
							<goal>enforce</goal>
						</goals>
						<configuration>
							<rules>
								<requireMavenVersion>
									<version>(,2.1.0),(2.1.0,2.2.0),(2.2.0,)</version>
									<message>Maven 2.1.0 and 2.2.0 produce incorrect GPG signatures and checksums respectively.</message>
								</requireMavenVersion>
							</rules>
						</configuration>
					</execution>
				</executions>
			</plugin>
		</plugins>
		<pluginManagement>
			<plugins>
				<plugin>
					<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
					<artifactId>maven-release-plugin</artifactId>
					<version>2.1</version>
					<configuration>
						<mavenExecutorId>forked-path</mavenExecutorId>
						<useReleaseProfile>false</useReleaseProfile>
						<arguments>-Psonatype-oss-release</arguments>
					</configuration>
				</plugin>
			</plugins>
		</pluginManagement>
	</build>

	<properties>
		<project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
		<sonatypeOssDistMgmtSnapshotsUrl>https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots/</sonatypeOssDistMgmtSnapshotsUrl>
	</properties>

	<profiles>
		<profile>
			<id>sonatype-oss-release</id>
			<build>
				<plugins>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>2.1.2</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>attach-sources</id>
								<goals>
									<goal>jar-no-fork</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>2.7</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>attach-javadocs</id>
								<goals>
									<goal>jar</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
					<plugin>
						<groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
						<artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
						<version>1.1</version>
						<executions>
							<execution>
								<id>sign-artifacts</id>
								<phase>verify</phase>
								<goals>
									<goal>sign</goal>
								</goals>
							</execution>
						</executions>
					</plugin>
				</plugins>
			</build>
		</profile>
	</profiles>

</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.sonatype.oss</groupId>
    <artifactId>oss-parent</artifactId>
    <version>7</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.8</version>

  <name>Compile Testing</name>
  <description>Utilities for testing compilation.</description>

  <url>http://github.com/google/compile-testing</url>
  <issueManagement>
    <system>GitHub</system>
    <url>http://github.com/google/compile-testing/issues</url>
  </issueManagement>
  <inceptionYear>2013</inceptionYear>
  <licenses>
    <license>
      <name>The Apache Software License, Version 2.0</name>
      <url>http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>
      <distribution>repo</distribution>
    </license>
  </licenses>
  <prerequisites>
    <maven>3.0.3</maven>
  </prerequisites>
  <scm>
    <connection>scm:git:http://github.com/google/compile-testing</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:git@github.com:google/compile-testing.git</developerConnection>
    <url>http://github.com/google/compile-testing</url>
    <tag>compile-testing-0.8</tag>
  </scm>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>16.0.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
      <version>${java.version}</version>
      <scope>system</scope>
      <systemPath>${toolsjar}</systemPath>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.code.findbugs</groupId>
      <artifactId>jsr305</artifactId>
      <version>1.3.9</version>
      <optional>true</optional>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.1</version>
        <configuration>
          <source>1.6</source>
          <target>1.6</target>
          <compilerArgument>-Xlint:all</compilerArgument>
          <showWarnings>true</showWarnings>
          <showDeprecation>true</showDeprecation>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-release-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5.1</version>
        <configuration>
          <releaseProfiles>release</releaseProfiles>
          <goals>deploy</goals>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
  <profiles>
    <profile>
      <id>default-profile</id>
      <activation>
        <activeByDefault>true</activeByDefault>
        <file>
          <exists>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</exists>
        </file>
      </activation>
      <properties>
        <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>
      </properties>
    </profile>
    <profile>

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
======================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Date: 2026-01-29

SUMMARY
-------
The Google Auto project build fails on Java 11 due to missing tools.jar dependency.
Three submodules are affected: factory, service, and value.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
The compile-testing library (versions 0.6 and 0.8) used for testing contains a
system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools:jar, which references tools.jar via the
${toolsjar} property.

In Java 8 and earlier, tools.jar existed at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar and
contained compiler APIs needed for annotation processing.

In Java 9+, tools.jar was removed as the Java Platform Module System (JPMS) was
introduced. The compiler APIs became part of the JDK modules and are automatically
available without requiring tools.jar.

The profiles in compile-testing POMs activate when tools.jar exists, setting the
toolsjar property. On Java 11, this file doesn't exist, but Maven still tries to
resolve the dependency, causing build failures.

AFFECTED MODULES
----------------
1. factory (auto-factory) - uses compile-testing 0.8
2. service (auto-service) - uses compile-testing 0.6
3. value (auto-value) - uses compile-testing 0.6 + missing auto-common 1.0-SNAPSHOT

DETAILED ERRORS
--------------
factory/pom.xml:
  - Error: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.8

service/pom.xml:
  - Error: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.6

value/pom.xml:
  - Error 1: Could not resolve dependencies for auto-common:1.0-SNAPSHOT
  - Error 2: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause 1: Missing SNAPSHOT dependency (needs to be built locally first)
  - Cause 2: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.6

SOLUTION STRATEGY
-----------------
The tools.jar dependency needs to be explicitly excluded from the compile-testing
transitive dependencies in all three submodules. This is safe to do because:

1. In Java 9+, the compiler APIs are available by default
2. compile-testing works without tools.jar on modern JVMs
3. The dependency is only used for compilation testing in test scope

Additionally, for the value module, auto-common needs to be built and installed
locally first.

FILES TO BE MODIFIED
-------------------
1. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/factory/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency

2. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/service/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency

3. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/value/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency
   - Fix auto-common dependency version from 1.0-SNAPSHOT to 0.3 or 0.5
     (or build auto-common locally first)

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH
-----------------------
For each module, add an <exclusions> block to the compile-testing dependency:

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>X.X</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>

This tells Maven to exclude the tools.jar dependency when resolving the
compile-testing dependency tree.

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
======================

Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto
Date: 2026-01-29

SUMMARY
-------
The Google Auto project build fails on Java 11 due to missing tools.jar dependency.
Three submodules are affected: factory, service, and value.

ROOT CAUSE
----------
The compile-testing library (versions 0.6 and 0.8) used for testing contains a
system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools:jar, which references tools.jar via the
${toolsjar} property.

In Java 8 and earlier, tools.jar existed at ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar and
contained compiler APIs needed for annotation processing.

In Java 9+, tools.jar was removed as the Java Platform Module System (JPMS) was
introduced. The compiler APIs became part of the JDK modules and are automatically
available without requiring tools.jar.

The profiles in compile-testing POMs activate when tools.jar exists, setting the
toolsjar property. On Java 11, this file doesn't exist, but Maven still tries to
resolve the dependency, causing build failures.

AFFECTED MODULES
----------------
1. factory (auto-factory) - uses compile-testing 0.8
2. service (auto-service) - uses compile-testing 0.6
3. value (auto-value) - uses compile-testing 0.6 + missing auto-common 1.0-SNAPSHOT

DETAILED ERRORS
--------------
factory/pom.xml:
  - Error: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.8

service/pom.xml:
  - Error: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.6

value/pom.xml:
  - Error 1: Could not resolve dependencies for auto-common:1.0-SNAPSHOT
  - Error 2: Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
    /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
  - Cause 1: Missing SNAPSHOT dependency (needs to be built locally first)
  - Cause 2: Transitive dependency from compile-testing:0.6

SOLUTION STRATEGY
-----------------
The tools.jar dependency needs to be explicitly excluded from the compile-testing
transitive dependencies in all three submodules. This is safe to do because:

1. In Java 9+, the compiler APIs are available by default
2. compile-testing works without tools.jar on modern JVMs
3. The dependency is only used for compilation testing in test scope

Additionally, for the value module, auto-common needs to be built and installed
locally first.

FILES TO BE MODIFIED
-------------------
1. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/factory/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency

2. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/service/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency

3. /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto/value/pom.xml
   - Add exclusion for com.sun:tools in compile-testing dependency
   - Fix auto-common dependency version from 1.0-SNAPSHOT to 0.3 or 0.5
     (or build auto-common locally first)

IMPLEMENTATION APPROACH
-----------------------
For each module, add an <exclusions> block to the compile-testing dependency:

<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>X.X</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>

This tells Maven to exclude the tools.jar dependency when resolving the
compile-testing dependency tree.

DIFFERENT errors that are beyond the scope of the original tools.jar build failure:
- factory needs javax.annotation.Generated compatibility fixes for Java 9+
- value needs auto-common 1.0-SNAPSHOT built locally or further API adjustments

The original build failure diagnosis and fix are complete and correct.
